back_translation: Everything has its season, and every matter under heaven has its time.
There is a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what was planted.
There is a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to tear down and a time to build.
There is a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance.
There is a time to throw stones away and a time to gather stones, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing.
There is a time to seek and a time to let be lost, a time to keep and a time to throw away.
There is a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be silent and a time to speak.
There is a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
What gain does the worker get from his toil?
I have seen the task that God has given to the sons of men to be occupied with.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet man still cannot fathom the work that God has done from beginning to end.
I realized that, for them, there is nothing better than to rejoice and to do good throughout their lives.
And that every man should eat, drink, and enjoy what is good in all his toil — this is a gift from God.
I realized that everything God does will endure forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing can be taken from it. God has done this so that men should fear Him.
What is has already been, and what will be has already been before, and God seeks out what has passed away.
Moreover, I saw under the sun that in the place of justice, wickedness was there, and in the place of righteousness, wickedness was there.
I said within my heart, “God will judge both the righteous and the wicked, for every matter and every deed has its time there.”
I said within my heart concerning the sons of men: God tests them so that they may see that they themselves are but beasts.

For what befalls the sons of men also befalls beasts — it is the same event. As one dies, so dies the other; all have the same breath. Man has nothing at all above the beasts, for everything is without substance.
All go to the same place; all come from the dust, and all return to the dust.
Who knows whether the spirit of man goes upward, and the spirit of the beast goes down to the earth below?
So I saw that there is nothing better than for a man to rejoice in his work, because that is his portion. For who can bring him to see what will happen after him?
